visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A young man with longish black hair and a dark gray bucket hat is seen in a close-up on a ferry boat. He wears a black graphic t-shirt. He points his right index finger toward a large poster on the white interior wall of the vessel. The poster contains colorful anime illustrations. The lighting is bright and natural, filtering through the ferry windows. (2) The scene shifts to the rear of a white passenger ferry docked at a concrete pier. A staff member in a white shirt and dark trousers walks across the boarding ramp. The background shows a wide river with small waves and a distant shoreline under an overcast sky. (3) The camera pans across a massive sand sculpture exhibition. A large central sculpture depicts various anime children and monsters. The man from the first phase appears in front of the sculpture, wearing a black backpack. He wipes sweat from his face and makes a peace sign with his hand. (4) Detailed montage of various individual sand sculptures. These include iconic monsters like a winged woman, a armored dragon with metal wings, a wolf-like creature, and several smaller creatures. The background transitions between the sand sculptures and the riverside park, with green trees and urban buildings visible in the distance. (5) The man stands before a giant sand sculpture of a female angel character with large wings. He gestures toward it with an open palm while looking into the camera. The sky has become slightly brighter with patches of blue. (6) A series of close-up and panning shots highlight the intricate textures of the sand sculptures, showing mechanical details on a metallic dragon and the organic forms of various characters. The video ends with a wide shot of a massive armored monster sculpture standing in the park.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video serves as a promotional vlog for the 2025 Bali City Sand Sculpture Exhibition in Taiwan. It specifically highlights the Digimon-themed sculptures. By using the iconic anime opening song 'Butter-Fly', the creator aims to evoke nostalgia and attract fans of the franchise to visit the park.
